title: Scaling the variables changes the loss geometry, not the dynamics: conditioning explains why one optimizer needs one step and another 60000
summary: A diagonal rescaling of the state leaves an ODE's eigenvalues unchanged but reweights the squared-error loss, which changes the curvature of the loss surface by a factor that can reach millions. These figures show the effect on the vector field, on a Runge-Kutta solver, on the loss surface and on how many iterations gradient descent and Adam need.

media.alt: Two panels. Left, titled paths in the normalized plane with d2 over d1 equal to 1000: grey elliptical level sets around a black star at (0.5, 0.5); a blue SGD-Z path and a yellow Adam-Z path go straight toward the star, while the raw paths hug the horizontal axis first. The legend lists iteration counts: SGD-R more than 60000, SGD-Z 1, Adam-R 50655, Adam-Z 73. Right, titled same loss, four ways to descend: loss ratio against iteration on log axes with four curves, three of them nearly flat for thousands of iterations.

read_the_figure.question: Is the optimizer slow because the problem is hard, or because the coordinates are badly scaled?
read_the_figure.axes: Left: the normalized coordinates z1 = y1/d1 and z2 = y2/d2 with level sets of the loss. Right: iteration (log, 1 to 1e5) against loss divided by initial loss (log, 1e-8 to 1). Scaling-law figure: scale ratio r = d2/d1 (log) against iterations to reach 1e-3 of the initial loss (log). Conditioning figures: loss surfaces over two parameters with the condition number in the title.
look_at: The iteration counts in the legend: the same loss and the same minimizer need 1 iteration (SGD in normalized coordinates), 73 (Adam normalized), 50655 (Adam raw) and over 60000 (SGD raw). Compare, do not average.
The raw loss surface (condition number 21628) is a very narrow valley; the normalized one (condition number 5.4) is a bowl. Level sets in the paths panel: solid raw, dashed normalized.
Scaling law: SGD raw rises with slope 2 in r, Adam raw with slope 0.86; both normalized curves are flat. Open triangles mark runs that did not reach the target in the budget.
Induced field: streamlines of the same spiral drawn for d2 = 1, 10, 100; the eigenvalues printed in each panel are identical (-0.25 +- 0.968 i) while the matrix norm grows from 1.3 to 10 to 100.

RK4 and affine maps: the maximum gap between running RK4 in y and in z = y/d is at round-off (1e-16) for a diagonal scaling but falls only like n^-4 for the nonlinear map z = log y; the adaptive-cost panel shows that the error norm, not the field, changes the cost.
Animation stills: induced field with d2 = 4 (norm 3.5), spectrum against norm (eigenvalues do not move), and four optimizer paths at iteration 35.
read_the_figure.proves: A change of variables y to D^{-1} y leaves the dynamics and spectrum unchanged but multiplies the loss Hessian by D^-2: it changes the cost of optimization by orders of magnitude and not the solution.
if_wrong: Iteration counts that grow like r squared: the loss is badly conditioned in the raw coordinates.
A loss that is flat for thousands of iterations while the minimizer is known: conditioning, not a bug.
RK4 results that differ between coordinates by more than round-off after an affine change: a bug.
A nonlinear transform treated as if it commuted with the solver: it does not.
must_check: That the scale ratio and the condition numbers are printed.
That the raw and normalized runs share the same minimizer and initial loss.
That iteration budgets are stated and unfinished runs are marked.
That the same tolerance convention is used when comparing raw and scaled runs.

terms.meaning: Divide each state component by a fixed scale d_i.
The right-hand side that the transformed variable obeys.
Largest over smallest curvature of the loss; gradient descent needs about this many iterations.
Plain gradient descent, and a method that rescales each coordinate by running gradient statistics.
The ratio of the scales of two state components, here r = d2/d1.

remember: Similar matrices have the same eigenvalues: D^{-1} J D has the spectrum of J.
Normalized MSE is raw MSE with weights 1/d_i^2.
Gradient descent on a quadratic needs about kappa iterations; kappa grows like r squared for scaling by r.
Adam partly undoes diagonal scaling, hence a smaller exponent (about 1).
Runge-Kutta methods commute with affine maps because each stage is a linear combination.

steps.title: The Jacobian under a diagonal scaling
steps.note: The eigenvalues are unchanged (the printed -0.25 +- 0.968 i) although the 2-norm changes; this is the induced-field panel for d2 = 1, 10, 100.

steps.title: Normalized MSE as a reweighting
steps.note: Dividing each residual by its scale multiplies the curvature along component i by d_i^-2; the ratio of the largest and smallest curvatures becomes r squared for two scales.

steps.title: Gradient descent iteration count
steps.note: For r = 100 so kappa = 1e4: N is about 35000, which is the order of the SGD-raw point at that r (computed here; the figure shows about 3e4).

steps.title: Why RK4 commutes with an affine map
steps.note: Each stage is a linear combination of previous stages and field values, so scaling passes through exactly; for z = log y the field is evaluated at nonlinearly related points and the two runs agree only to O(h^4).

worked.title: Iterations of gradient descent at scale ratio 100
worked.problem: Two coordinates with scale ratio r = 100 give a raw condition number about r squared. Estimate the iterations to reduce the loss by a factor 1e-3 at the best step size.
worked.answer: About 35000, in line with the SGD-raw point at r = 100 in the scaling plot (about 3e4); after normalization kappa is 1 and one step suffices.

analyze.q: The eigenvalues printed in the three induced-field panels are identical but the norms differ. Which of the two controls the stability limit of an explicit solver, and which controls the condition of the MSE?
Why is Adam's slope in the scaling law smaller than SGD's, and why is it still not zero?
Why does the nonlinear log map not commute with RK4?
analyze.hint: Stages evaluated at nonlinearly related points.

evaluate.q: A report says 'normalization made Adam 700 times faster'. What is the fair statement?
evaluate.hint: Same loss and minimizer, different coordinates.

evaluate.q: Is the normalized loss the same objective as the raw loss? What does each emphasize?

create: Choose scales d_i for a three-component state and write the weights of the raw MSE that the normalized loss implies.
Extend the scaling law to three scales and predict the exponent for SGD.

checks.q: What stays unchanged under a diagonal rescaling of the state?
checks.answer: The eigenvalues of the Jacobian at any point, the trajectory (as a set) and the minimizer of the loss; the Hessian does not stay.

checks.q: Scale ratio 30. Condition number of the raw MSE and iterations for gradient descent (factor 1e-3)?
Why does SGD raw scale like r squared but Adam like r?
checks.answer: Gradient descent needs kappa = r^2 steps; Adam's per-coordinate normalization divides the step by the gradient size, removing one power of r.

checks.q: RK4 gives the same answer in y and in z = y/d to 1e-16. Does that show the loss is the same?
checks.answer: No: it shows the dynamics commute with the scaling; the loss changes because the residuals are weighted differently.

checks.q: Design an experiment that separates the effect of scaling on the solver from its effect on the optimizer.
checks.answer: Fix the optimizer and vary the error norm in the adaptive solver (affects NFE), then fix the solver and vary the loss weights (affects iterations).
